title: Cabin and Flight Interphone Audio Quality and Spares Availability
abstract: Operator request for a replacement of the analogue interphone amplifier after a run of unreadable cabin-to-cockpit calls and a supplier notice withdrawing the repair capability for the existing unit.

sections.request: Our cabin crew have been reporting for about a year that calls from the aft galley to the flight deck are hard to understand, with a hum underneath the speech that gets worse as the flight goes on. It is not every aircraft and it is not every flight, but it is often enough that the crews have started using their mobile handsets on the ground instead, which we do not want. Separately our supplier has written to tell us that the amplifier can no longer be repaired and that we should plan for replacement. We would like one solution that fixes the audio quality and gives us a unit we can still buy, and we would prefer it to be something our own shop can fit rather than a full rewire.
sections.background: We have twenty-two aircraft on the affected standard. The audio complaint was first raised in 2024 and a wiring check bulletin was carried out on six aircraft with no finding. Our reliability figures show fourteen amplifier removals in eighteen months against a fleet expectation of four, and the shop reports that eleven of the fourteen tested serviceable. The supplier withdrawal notice is dated February 2026 and gives a last-order date of June 2027.
sections.expected_outcome: Intelligible cabin-to-cockpit and cabin-to-cabin calls in every seat position, an amplifier with a supported repair route, and an embodiment that can be done overnight without disturbing the cabin lining.

type_data.business_justification: Fourteen removals in eighteen months against an expectation of four, eleven of them no-fault-found, combined with a supplier last-order date of June 2027 that leaves no spares route beyond that point.
